price-index.def: A number that compares the cost of a fixed market basket of goods in one year with its cost in a base year, where the index equals 100.

cpi.def: Consumer price index: the cost of a basket of goods and services that typical households buy, divided by its cost in the base year, times 100.

inflation.def: A rise in prices in general across the economy. The inflation rate is the percent change in a price index from one period to the next.

deflation.def: A fall in prices in general, so the inflation rate is negative. Disinflation is different: inflation slows, but prices are still rising.

substitution-bias.def: The overstatement of inflation by a fixed-basket index when people switch from goods whose prices rose to cheaper substitutes.

real-value.def: A nominal value (in dollars of the day) adjusted for prices: nominal value divided by a price index, times 100. A real wage is what a nominal wage buys in base-year dollars.
